subject: Finlytics discovery — monthly spend corridor & procurement path (recap)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Finlytics discovery — monthly spend corridor & procurement path (recap)

Alex — thanks again for the 30-minute call this morning. Below is a short recap and a proposal for next steps so your procurement and engineering teams can evaluate internally.

Key notes from the call:
- Workload: real-time scoring for customer journeys (avg. prompt length ~350 tokens, peak concurrency ~60 requests/s).
- Traffic shape: steady-state ~45M tokens/month, expected ramp to 120M tokens/month over 3–6 months with seasonal spikes.
- Sensitivity: latency SLOs at 200–250ms p50 for single-turn generation.

Budget & pricing signals (we discussed ranges, see validation ask below):
- Early pilot expected spend band: $20k — $60k / month.
- Target unit economics we talked through: goal is roughly $700–$1,000 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot (depends on batching & KV cache hit rates).

Procurement constraints you mentioned:
- Small POs (< $15k) are handled by the payments team; anything above requires a formal PO + 45–60 day finance SLA.
- Security pack (SOC2, data retention) will be requested if we move to a dedicated environment.

Requested confirmation from your side (quick ask):
1) Can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly burn band (low / expected / high) — e.g., 40M / 75M / 120M tokens?
2) Procurement threshold that triggers a PO vs. payment by credit card (your note said ~15k but wanted explicit ladder).
3) Is a 45–60 day finance lead time acceptable for pilot PO?

Proposed next steps:
- I will pull together a short pricing sketch for the three burn scenarios (low/typical/high) and a procurement playbook variant based on your thresholds — target to send by Tuesday EOD (Oct 6).
- If procurement prefers, we can schedule a 30-minute call with our finance ops to walk through PO cadence and payment options.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager procurement playbook and a sample PO template for quick review.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0193

Jordan — thanks for the recap, looks good. Two quick clarifications so procurement can triage: 

1) Unit economics: can you provide an example line-item that maps to $/1M tokens with our expected prompt shapes? I want something I can hand to finance that shows the math (tokens, batching assumptions, avg tokens/req).

2) Procurement ladder: you wrote ~15k — for us the thresholds are: <$10k by credit card, $10k–$50k PO with standard 45d net, >$50k requires legal review + signed SOW. Can you confirm you can support that split and whether Redwood offers a short-term pilot PO (under $50k) with standard terms?

If you can send the pricing sketch and a recommended PO path (who signs, expected lead times) that will let procurement decide if we can fast-track.

—Alex

Quick internal note / recommended approach for Jordan to share back: 

- Pricing sketch: prepare 3 scenarios mapped to token bands: 40M / 75M / 120M tokens per month. Use conservative batching (avg tokens per request = 420, cache hit assumed 10% for prefix) for the pilot pricing sample. That will produce a unit cost delta but keeps expectations conservative for finance.
- Suggested $/1M target to present: provide two columns — (1) list price per 1M tokens and (2) an illustrative pilot commit discount. Example: List: $1,050 / 1M; Pilot (commit 3 mo): $820 / 1M. 
- Procurement ladder: mirror what Alex wrote but confirm our internal gating: we can accept CC for <$10k, PO up to $50k with standard 45d net; anything >$50k needs legal + security review (and likely Dedicated discussion).
- PO template: attach the v2 playbook and the sample PO we prefer procurement to use. If procurement needs DocuSign, we can provide.

I'll let you draft the email back to Alex; include the sample math and attach the two files. If they show >$50k intent we should offer a short procurement call next week so legal/security can scope.

Marissa
VP, Growth Ops (Sales Enablement)
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-procurement-playbook_v2.pdf (procurement playbook, 2 pages), finlytics-mopp-reviewed.xlsx (simple cost calc).

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@finlytics.com
Date: 2026-10-06T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finlytics discovery — monthly spend corridor & procurement path (recap)

Alex — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a short pricing sketch and the PO template. Below is the condensed answer you can share with finance: 

1) Pilot pricing sketch (conservative assumptions) — illustrative only:
- Scenario A (low): 40M tokens / month -> list compute + infra = $1,050 per 1M tokens -> monthly cost ≈ $42,000.
- Scenario B (expected): 75M tokens / month -> list $1,050 / 1M -> monthly cost ≈ $78,750. Pilot commit discount (3-month): $820 per 1M -> monthly cost ≈ $61,500 on Scenario B.
- Scenario C (high): 120M tokens / month -> list $1,050 / 1M -> monthly cost ≈ $126,000. With engineering-level batching & caching optimizations we’ve seen effective $/1M as low as $600 for long-running customers — we’ll include tuning notes in the playbook.

Notes on assumptions: avg tokens/request = 420; cache hit = 10%; continuous batching improvements during pilot could reduce per-1M token cost. These details are in the attached calc.

2) Procurement ladder & Redwood stance:
- < $10k: credit card (self-serve) — immediate.
- $10k–$50k: PO accepted, standard 45d net. We can support pilot POs in this band without extra legal; finance ops will process via our standard PO flow.
- > $50k: requires legal review and security checklist (SOC2 evidence / data retention discussion). For >$75k we recommend exploring a Dedicated commitment discussion (reserved capacity) — that shifts contract model and billing cadence.

3) Lead times: PO processing is typically 7–14 business days once the PO is received; legal review can add 2–3 weeks depending on redlines. If you need a faster path we can accept an initial PO for the lower band and a follow-on SOW for the larger commit.

Next steps we propose:
- I’ll drop the pricing sketch (attached) and the PO template for procurement.
- If procurement confirms they can fast-track a $10k–$50k PO, can we aim to sign within the next 14 business days? If so, please let me know the PO contact and I’ll loop our finance ops.
- Optional: schedule a 30-minute procurement ops call next week — I can bring Marissa and our finance ops lead to answer questions live.

Attachments: redwood-procurement-playbook_v2.pdf (procurement playbook + tuning notes), finlytics-mopp-reviewed.xlsx (token math).

Thanks — Jordan
